title: Classic Spaghetti Carbonara
description: Silky Roman pasta with crisp guanciale, eggs, and Pecorino — no cream.

ingredients.name: kosher salt, for the pasta water

steps.instructionText: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the salt.
Cook the guanciale in a dry skillet over medium heat until crisp and the fat has rendered.
Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, Pecorino, and pepper together in a bowl.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.
Off the heat, toss the pasta with the guanciale, then stir in the egg mixture, adding pasta water a splash at a time until glossy. Serve immediately.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Yogurt-marinated chicken simmered in a spiced tomato-cream sauce.

steps.instructionText: Combine the yogurt, half the garam masala, cumin, half the garlic, and the ginger. Add the chicken and marinate in the fridge.
Spread the chicken on a sheet pan and broil until charred in spots.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft.
Add the remaining garlic and garam masala and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes and simmer, then add the cream and the chicken.
Simmer until the chicken is cooked through. Garnish with cilantro.

title: Overnight Oats
description: Creamy no-cook oats you stir together the night before.

steps.instructionText: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, maple syrup, vanilla, and salt together in a jar.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Top with blueberries and eat cold, or warm for a minute in the microwave.

title: Beef & Guinness Stew
description: Slow-braised Irish stew with tender beef, root vegetables, and a dark stout gravy.

steps.instructionText: Toss the beef with the flour and a generous pinch of salt and pepper.
Brown the beef in batches in the oil in a Dutch oven. Set aside.
Cook the onions, carrots, and celery in the same pot until softened.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the Guinness, scraping up the browned bits, then add the broth, thyme, bay leaves, and beef.
Cover and simmer gently until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer uncovered until tender and the gravy has thickened. Remove the bay leaves before serving.

title: Vegan Black Bean Tacos
description: Smoky black beans, avocado, and quick-pickled onion in warm corn tortillas.

steps.instructionText: Toss the onion with the juice of one lime and a pinch of salt; set aside to pickle.
Warm the beans with the chili powder, cumin, and a splash of water, mashing lightly.
Char the tortillas in a dry skillet.
Fill the tortillas with beans, sliced avocado, pickled onion, salsa verde, and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

title: Grandma's Buttermilk Pancakes
description: Tall, fluffy, diner-style pancakes.

steps.instructionText: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs, and melted butter.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir until just combined — a few lumps are fine.
Cook ¼-cup portions on a buttered griddle over medium heat until bubbles form, then flip.

title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken
description: Fragrant coconut curry with chicken, bamboo shoots, and Thai basil.

steps.instructionText: Start the jasmine rice.
Fry the curry paste in a few spoonfuls of the thick coconut cream until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir until coated.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, the lime leaves, fish sauce, and sugar, and simmer.
Add the bamboo shoots and pepper and cook until just tender. Stir in the basil and serve over rice.

title: Caprese Salad
description: Ripe tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and basil — a summer classic.

steps.instructionText: Slice the tomatoes and mozzarella and arrange them on a platter, alternating with basil leaves.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic glaze and sprinkle with flaky salt.

title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork
description: Sweet-and-smoky shredded pork for sandwiches.

steps.instructionText: Rub the pork all over with the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, and a big pinch of salt.
Put the onion in the slow cooker, set the pork on top, and pour in the vinegar.
Cover and cook on LOW until the pork falls apart.
Shred with two forks, stir in barbecue sauce to taste, and pile onto buns.

title: Miso Soup
description: A light, savory Japanese soup with tofu and wakame.

steps.instructionText: Soak the kombu in the water, then bring it just to a simmer and remove the kombu.
Add the wakame and tofu and warm through.
Turn off the heat. Whisk the miso with a ladle of broth, then stir it back into the pot — don't let it boil.
Serve topped with scallions.

title: French Onion Soup
description: Deeply caramelized onions in rich broth under a lid of bubbling Gruyère.

steps.instructionText: Melt the butter in a Dutch oven, add the onions and sugar, and cook, stirring occasionally, until deep golden brown.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Add the broth, thyme, and bay leaf and simmer.
Toast the baguette slices under the broiler.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls on a baking sheet and top with the toast and Gruyère.
Broil until the cheese is melted and bubbling.

title: Crème Brûlée
description: Vanilla custard under a shatteringly crisp caramel top.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 325°F. Warm the cream with the vanilla bean until steaming, then let it steep.
Whisk the egg yolks, ½ cup sugar, and salt until pale, then slowly whisk in the warm cream.
Strain into the ramekins and set them in a roasting pan. Pour hot water halfway up their sides.
Bake until set at the edges but still jiggly in the center.
Chill until cold.
Sprinkle each with 1 tablespoon sugar and caramelize with a torch just before serving.

title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Chewy in the middle, crisp at the edges.

steps.instructionText: Whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt together.
Beat the butter and both sugars until light and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Mix in the dry ingredients on low, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Chill the dough.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Scoop onto lined baking sheets and bake until golden at the edges.
Shake everything together in a jar until emulsified. Keeps for a week in the fridge.

title: Instant Pot Chicken Noodle Soup
description: Comforting homemade chicken soup in under an hour.

steps.instructionText: Sauté the onion, carrots, and celery in the Instant Pot until softened.
Add the garlic, thyme, chicken, and broth.
Pressure cook on HIGH, then quick release.
Shred the chicken with two forks.
Stir in the noodles and cook on Sauté until tender. Finish with parsley.

title: Korean Beef Bulgogi
description: Thin-sliced beef in a sweet soy, pear, and sesame marinade.

steps.instructionText: Mix the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, pear, garlic, ginger, and half the scallions.
Add the beef, toss to coat, and marinate in the fridge.
Sear the beef in batches in a very hot skillet until caramelized.
Top with the remaining scallions and sesame seeds and serve with rice.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced pepper-and-tomato sauce.

steps.instructionText: Cook the onion and pepper in the oil until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, and paprika and cook until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and simmer until slightly thickened.
Make six wells, crack an egg into each, cover, and cook until the whites are set.
Scatter with feta and parsley and serve with crusty bread.

title: Herb-Brined Roast Turkey with Pan Gravy
description: A juicy holiday turkey: brined overnight, roasted with herb butter, served with pan gravy.

steps.instructionText: Dissolve the salt and brown sugar in the water with half the herbs and the peppercorns. Cool completely.
Submerge the turkey in the brine and refrigerate.
Remove the turkey, rinse, and pat very dry. Heat the oven to 425°F.
Mash the butter with the remaining chopped herbs and rub it under and over the skin.
Stuff the cavity with the lemons, onions, and garlic, and set the turkey on a rack in the roasting pan.
Roast for 30 minutes, then lower the oven to 350°F and roast until the thigh reaches 165°F.
Rest the turkey, loosely tented with foil.
Skim the pan drippings, whisk in the flour, then the stock, and simmer into gravy while the turkey rests.

title: Mango Lassi
description: A cool, creamy yogurt-and-mango drink.

steps.instructionText: Blend everything until smooth and frothy, then pour into glasses.

title: Weeknight Mac & Cheese
description: Creamy stovetop mac and cheese, no oven required.

steps.instructionText: Cook the macaroni until just al dente and drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the milk and simmer until thickened.
Off the heat, stir in the cheddar, American cheese, Parmesan, mustard, hot sauce, and salt until smooth.
Fold in the macaroni and serve right away.

title: Classic French Toast
description: Thick brioche soaked in cinnamon custard and griddled until golden.

steps.instructionText: Whisk the eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt in a shallow dish.
Soak each brioche slice for about 20 seconds per side.
Melt a little butter on a griddle over medium heat and cook the slices until golden, 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Serve hot with maple syrup.

title: Huevos Rancheros
description: Fried eggs on crisp corn tortillas with black beans and a quick ranchero sauce.

steps.instructionText: Cook the onion and jalapeño in 1 tablespoon of oil until soft, then add the garlic and cumin.
Add the tomatoes, simmer until slightly thickened, then blend until mostly smooth.
Meanwhile, warm the black beans in a small saucepan.
Fry the tortillas in the remaining oil until crisp at the edges.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in the same pan.
Top two tortillas per plate with beans, two eggs, sauce, queso fresco, avocado, and cilantro.

title: Avocado Toast with Poached Egg
description: Smashed avocado on toasted sourdough topped with a soft poached egg.

steps.instructionText: Bring a saucepan of water and the vinegar to a gentle simmer.
Crack in the eggs and poach until the whites are set but the yolks are runny.
Meanwhile, toast the bread and mash the avocado with the lemon juice and a little salt.
Spread the avocado on the toast, top each with an egg, and finish with pepper flakes and flaky salt.

title: Blueberry Muffins
description: Bakery-style muffins with crackly sugar tops that freeze well for busy mornings.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 400°F and line the muffin tin.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, oil, and vanilla, stir into the dry ingredients until just combined, then fold in the blueberries.
Divide the batter among the cups and sprinkle with turbinado sugar.
Bake until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the tin before serving, or cool completely and freeze.

title: Spinach & Feta Frittata
description: A one-pan egg bake that is just as good cold the next day.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 375°F and whisk the eggs, milk, salt, and pepper.
Cook the shallot in the oil until soft.
Add the spinach and stir until wilted.
Pour in the eggs, scatter over the tomatoes and feta, and cook on the stove until the edges set.
Bake until the center is just set.
Rest, then cut into wedges.

title: Freezer Breakfast Burritos
description: Sausage, egg, and potato burritos to roll in a batch and reheat all week.

steps.instructionText: Brown the sausage in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the hash browns and cook until crisp.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt, and pepper, add to the pan, and scramble until just set.
Warm the tortillas so they fold without cracking.
Fill each tortilla with the egg mixture, cheese, and a spoonful of salsa, then roll tightly.
Serve now, or wrap each burrito in foil and freeze for up to 3 months; reheat from frozen at 350°F for about 30 minutes.

title: Greek Yogurt Parfait
description: Layers of yogurt, granola, berries, and honey in five minutes.

steps.instructionText: Spoon half the yogurt into a glass and top with half the granola and berries.
Repeat the layers.
Drizzle with honey, sprinkle with almonds, and eat right away so the granola stays crunchy.

title: Tofu Scramble
description: A turmeric-golden vegan scramble with peppers and spinach.

steps.instructionText: Cook the onion and pepper in the oil until soft.
Crumble the tofu into the pan and stir in the turmeric, nutritional yeast, and garlic powder.
Fold in the spinach until wilted.
Season with black salt and pepper and serve.

title: Belgian Waffles
description: Crisp outside and airy inside, thanks to whipped egg whites.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the waffle iron.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk the egg yolks, milk, melted butter, and vanilla, then stir into the dry ingredients.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the batter.
Cook the batter in the waffle iron until deep golden and crisp.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve with fruit.

title: Eggs Benedict
description: Poached eggs and Canadian bacon on English muffins under a blender hollandaise.

steps.instructionText: Blend the yolks, lemon juice, and cayenne, then stream in hot melted butter with the blender running until thick. Keep warm.
Brown the Canadian bacon in a skillet.
Toast the English muffin halves.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar, in batches.
Top each muffin half with bacon, an egg, hollandaise, and snipped chives.

title: Chicken Congee
description: Silky Chinese rice porridge with ginger and shredded chicken for a slow weekend morning.

steps.instructionText: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear.
Bring the rice, stock, water, and ginger to a boil in a Dutch oven.
Add the chicken, lower to a gentle simmer, and cook partly covered until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove and shred the chicken; keep simmering the rice, stirring often, until broken down and creamy.
Stir the chicken back in and season with salt and white pepper.
Serve topped with scallions, a drizzle of sesame oil, and fried shallots.

title: Baked Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal
description: A sliceable oat bake that reheats well all week.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter the baking dish.
Mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt.
Whisk the milk, eggs, maple syrup, and melted butter, pour over the oats, and fold in the apples and half the walnuts.
Spread in the dish, top with the remaining walnuts, and bake until set and golden.
Serve warm, or refrigerate for up to 5 days and reheat by the slice.

title: Full English Breakfast
description: Sausages, bacon, eggs, beans, mushrooms, and tomatoes: the classic weekend fry-up.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 200°F to keep everything warm as it finishes.
Fry the sausages in the oil over medium heat, turning often.
Add the bacon and black pudding to the pan and cook until crisp, then move everything to the oven.
Fry the mushrooms in the butter, with the tomatoes cut-side down alongside.
Meanwhile, warm the beans in a small saucepan.
Fry the eggs and toast the bread.
Plate everything together and serve at once.

title: Kanda Poha
description: Mumbai-style flattened rice with onion, mustard seeds, turmeric, and peanuts.

steps.instructionText: Rinse the poha briefly in a colander, drain well, and toss with the sugar and salt.
Fry the peanuts in the oil until golden, then lift them out.
Add the mustard seeds; when they pop, add the curry leaves and chilies.
Add the onion and turmeric and cook until soft.
Add the poha and peanuts and toss over low heat until hot.
Finish with lemon juice and cilantro.

title: Berry Smoothie Bowl
description: A thick frozen berry and banana bowl you eat with a spoon.

steps.instructionText: Blend the berries, banana, and almond milk until thick and smooth, scraping down the sides; add a splash more milk only if needed.
Spoon into a bowl and top with kiwi, coconut, chia seeds, and hemp hearts. Eat immediately.

title: Tamagoyaki
description: Sweet-savory Japanese rolled omelet, great for breakfast or a bento.

steps.instructionText: Beat the eggs with the dashi, sugar, soy sauce, mirin, and salt without making them foamy.
Oil the pan over medium-low heat, pour in a thin layer, and roll it toward you when nearly set.
Push the roll to the far side, oil the pan, and add another thin layer, lifting the roll so egg flows underneath; roll back. Repeat until the egg is used up.
Shape the omelet in a bamboo mat, then slice into six pieces.

title: Overnight Sausage & Egg Breakfast Casserole
description: Assemble it the night before and bake in the morning; made for holiday brunch.

steps.instructionText: Brown the sausage in a skillet, breaking it up, then drain.
Grease the baking dish and layer in the bread, sausage, cheese, and green onions.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard, salt, and pepper, pour over the bread, and press down so it soaks.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Bake uncovered at 350°F until puffed and set in the center.
Rest before cutting.

title: Classic Club Sandwich
description: Triple-decker toast with roast turkey, crisp bacon, lettuce, and tomato.

steps.instructionText: Cook the bacon until crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Toast the bread.
Spread mayonnaise on one side of each slice of toast.
Layer toast, turkey, lettuce, toast, bacon, tomato, and a final slice of toast; season with pepper.
Secure each sandwich with four toothpicks and cut into quarters on the diagonal.

title: Chicken Caesar Salad
description: Crisp romaine, seared chicken, garlicky croutons, and a punchy homemade dressing.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Toss the bread cubes with 2 tablespoons of the oil and bake until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, season the chicken and sear it in 1 tablespoon of oil until cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes per side; rest, then slice.
Whisk the garlic, anchovies, mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, and Worcestershire, then whisk in the remaining oil and half the Parmesan.
Toss the chopped romaine with the dressing, then top with the chicken, croutons, and remaining Parmesan.

title: Greek Salad
description: Chunky tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and a slab of feta, with no lettuce in sight.

steps.instructionText: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, onion, and olives in a bowl and season with salt.
Lay the block of feta on top.
Drizzle with the oil and vinegar, sprinkle with oregano, and serve with crusty bread.

title: Tomato Soup & Grilled Cheese
description: Creamy tomato-basil soup with crisp, melty grilled cheese for dunking.

steps.instructionText: Melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in a Dutch oven and cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, broth, sugar, and salt and simmer.
Add the basil leaves, blend until smooth, and stir in the cream.
Butter the outsides of the bread, fill with cheddar, and griddle over medium heat until golden and melted.
Cut the sandwiches in half and serve with the soup.

title: Chicken Quesadillas
description: Crisp tortillas stuffed with chicken, peppers, and plenty of melted cheese.

steps.instructionText: Cook the pepper in a little oil until just soft.
Toss the chicken with the chili powder and cooked pepper.
Cover half of each tortilla with cheese, chicken, and green onions, then fold over.
Cook the quesadillas in a lightly oiled skillet until golden and melted, 2 to 3 minutes per side, in batches.
Cut into wedges and serve with sour cream and salsa.

title: Lemongrass Chicken Banh Mi
description: Vietnamese baguette sandwiches with caramelized lemongrass chicken, quick pickles, and herbs.

steps.instructionText: Toss the chicken with the lemongrass, fish sauce, brown sugar, and garlic and marinate.
Meanwhile, stir the carrot and daikon with the vinegar, sugar, and salt and leave to pickle.
Grill the chicken over medium-high heat until charred and cooked through, then slice.
Stir the mayonnaise and sriracha together.
Split the baguettes, spread with sriracha mayo, and fill with chicken, drained pickles, cucumber, jalapeño, and cilantro.

title: Falafel Pitas with Tahini Sauce
description: Crisp, herby falafel made from soaked dried chickpeas, tucked into warm pitas.

steps.instructionText: Cover the chickpeas with cold water by 2 inches and soak.
Drain well, then pulse with the onion, garlic, herbs, spices, and salt until finely chopped but not a paste. Stir in the baking soda.
Shape into about 24 small patties.
Heat the oil to 350°F and fry the falafel in batches until deep brown.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, ⅓ cup water, and a pinch of salt into a pourable sauce.
Fill the warm pitas with falafel, tomato, cucumber, and tahini sauce.

title: Mediterranean Quinoa Meal-Prep Bowls
description: Four grab-and-go lunches of quinoa, roasted chickpeas, vegetables, and lemon dressing.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the chickpeas with 1 tablespoon of oil, the paprika, and a pinch of salt and roast until crisp.
Meanwhile, simmer the quinoa in the water, covered, for 15 minutes, then fluff and cool.
Whisk the remaining oil with the lemon juice, oregano, and salt.
Divide the quinoa, chickpeas, vegetables, olives, and feta among four containers, with the dressing on the side. Refrigerate for up to 4 days.

title: Cobb Salad
description: Rows of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato, and blue cheese over crisp greens.

steps.instructionText: Cover the eggs with water, bring to a boil, and simmer until hard-cooked.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon until crisp and crumble it.
Cool the eggs in ice water, then peel and chop.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard, oil, salt, and pepper.
Arrange the chopped romaine on a platter and lay the chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomatoes, and blue cheese over it in rows. Drizzle with dressing.

title: Tuna Melt
description: Open-faced tuna salad on rye, broiled under sharp cheddar.

steps.instructionText: Heat the broiler.
Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, celery, onion, lemon juice, and pepper.
Toast the bread under the broiler, about a minute per side.
Spread with the tuna, top with cheddar, and broil until bubbling.

title: Cold Sesame Noodles
description: Chewy noodles in a creamy sesame-peanut sauce; even better after a night in the fridge.

steps.instructionText: Boil the noodles according to the package directions.
Rinse under cold water, drain well, and toss with a little of the sesame oil.
Whisk the tahini, peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, remaining sesame oil, maple syrup, chili crisp, ginger, and garlic with 2 to 3 tablespoons of hot water.
Toss the noodles with the sauce and top with cucumber, scallions, and sesame seeds. Eat now or refrigerate for up to 3 days.

title: Turkish Red Lentil Soup
description: Silky red lentil soup (mercimek çorbası) with a sizzling Aleppo pepper oil.

steps.instructionText: Cook the onion and carrot in 2 tablespoons of the oil until soft.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, and cumin.
Add the lentils and broth and simmer until the lentils fall apart.
Blend until smooth and season with salt.
Warm the remaining oil with the Aleppo pepper, drizzle over each bowl, and serve with lemon wedges. Freezes well.

title: Chicken Shawarma Wraps
description: Spiced, charred chicken wrapped in flatbread with garlic yogurt sauce and pickles.

steps.instructionText: Toss the chicken with the plain yogurt, 2 tablespoons of the lemon juice, 3 cloves of garlic, the spices, salt, and 1 tablespoon of oil, then marinate in the fridge.
Sear the chicken in the remaining oil over medium-high heat, in batches, until charred and cooked through.
Rest the chicken, then slice thinly.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the remaining garlic and lemon juice.
Fill the flatbreads with romaine, tomato, pickles, chicken, and garlic sauce, then roll up tightly.

title: Muffuletta
description: New Orleans pressed sandwich of Italian meats, provolone, and olive salad, made to feed a crowd.

steps.instructionText: Mix the giardiniera, olives, capers, oil, vinegar, and oregano to make the olive salad.
Split the loaf horizontally and pull out a little of the soft crumb.
Spread half the olive salad on the bottom, layer on the meats and provolone, then the rest of the olive salad, and replace the top.
Wrap tightly in plastic and press under a heavy skillet in the fridge.
Cut into 8 wedges. It can be made up to a day ahead.

title: Ahi Poke Bowls
description: Sushi-grade tuna in a soy-sesame marinade over seasoned rice.

steps.instructionText: Cook the rice.
Let the rice rest, then fold in the vinegar.
Meanwhile, toss the tuna with the soy sauce, sesame oil, green onions, and ginger and chill.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the tuna, avocado, cucumber, edamame, and sesame seeds.

title: Black Bean Burrito Bowls
description: Cilantro-lime rice, spiced black beans, charred corn, and avocado; packs up for the week.

steps.instructionText: Simmer the rice in the salted water, covered, until tender.
Char the corn in 1 tablespoon of oil in a hot skillet.
Meanwhile, warm the beans with the cumin, chili powder, remaining oil, and a splash of water.
Fluff the rice with the juice of one lime and chopped cilantro.
Toss the corn with the onion, tomatoes, and remaining lime juice.
Divide the rice, beans, and corn salsa among bowls and top with avocado just before eating. Keeps for 4 days without the avocado.

title: Slow Cooker White Chicken Chili
description: Creamy white bean and green chile chili that simmers all morning.

steps.instructionText: Put the chicken, beans, chiles, onion, garlic, spices, salt, and broth in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low.
Shred the chicken with two forks and return it to the pot.
Stir in the cream cheese and corn and cook until melted and creamy.
Finish with lime juice and cilantro. Freezes well in lunch-size portions.

title: Egg Salad Sandwiches
description: Creamy, chive-flecked egg salad on soft bread; the filling keeps for three days.

steps.instructionText: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to a boil, then cover, take off the heat, and let stand.
Chill the eggs in ice water.
Peel and chop the eggs, then mix with the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, celery, chives, salt, and paprika.
Spread onto four slices of bread, add lettuce, and top with the remaining bread.

title: Instant Pot Butternut Squash Soup
description: Velvety squash soup with apple and warm spices, ready in under an hour.

steps.instructionText: Use the sauté setting to cook the onion in the oil until soft.
Add the garlic, cinnamon, and nutmeg and stir for a minute.
Add the squash, apple, and broth, lock the lid, and pressure cook on high. It takes about 10 minutes to come up to pressure.
Let the pressure release naturally.
Blend until smooth, stir in the coconut milk and salt, and top with pumpkin seeds.

title: Thai Chicken Larb Lettuce Wraps
description: Zesty minced chicken with lime, fish sauce, fresh herbs, and toasted rice in lettuce cups.

steps.instructionText: Toast the rice in a dry skillet until golden, then grind to a coarse powder.
Cook the chicken with a splash of water, breaking it up, until no longer pink.
Off the heat, stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, pepper flakes, and shallots.
Fold in the mint, cilantro, green onions, and toasted rice powder.
Spoon into lettuce cups to serve.

title: Classic Hummus with Veggie Sticks
description: Ultra-smooth hummus with carrot, cucumber, and pepper sticks for dipping.

steps.instructionText: Blend the tahini and lemon juice for a minute until whipped and pale.
Add the garlic, cumin, salt, and chickpeas and blend, scraping down the sides and streaming in the ice water, until very smooth.
Spread in a shallow bowl and finish with the olive oil and paprika.
Cut the vegetables into sticks and serve alongside. The hummus keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

title: Fresh Guacamole with Tortilla Chips
description: Chunky, lime-bright guacamole made right before serving.

steps.instructionText: Mash the onion and jalapeño with a pinch of the salt into a rough paste.
Add the avocados and mash, leaving plenty of chunks.
Fold in the tomato, cilantro, lime juice, and the rest of the salt to taste.
Serve right away with the chips.

title: Parmesan Herb Popcorn
description: Stovetop popcorn tossed with butter, Parmesan, and dried herbs.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oil with 3 kernels in a covered pot over medium-high heat until they pop.
Add the remaining kernels, cover, and shake the pot often until the popping slows to 2 or 3 seconds apart.
Tip the popcorn into a large bowl and melt the butter in the warm pot.
Toss the popcorn with the butter, Parmesan, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, and salt.

title: Peanut Butter Energy Bites
description: No-bake oat bites with peanut butter, honey, flax, and mini chocolate chips.

steps.instructionText: Stir all the ingredients together until evenly combined.
Chill the mixture so it is easier to roll.
Roll into 20 balls.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to a week.

title: Crispy Roasted Chickpeas
description: Crunchy, smoky chickpeas to eat by the handful.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Dry the chickpeas thoroughly in a towel, discarding any loose skins.
Roast the chickpeas plain on a baking sheet.
Toss with the oil, spices, and salt and roast until deep golden and crunchy.
Cool on the sheet so they crisp further.
Store uncovered at room temperature for up to 2 days.

title: Classic Deviled Eggs
description: Creamy, tangy yolk filling piped into egg whites and dusted with smoked paprika.

steps.instructionText: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to a boil, then cover, take off the heat, and let stand.
Chill the eggs in ice water.
Peel and halve the eggs lengthwise, and pop the yolks into a bowl.
Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, and salt until smooth.
Pipe the filling into the whites, then dust with paprika and snipped chives.

title: Chewy Granola Bars
description: Honey-sweetened oat bars with almonds and dried cranberries, far better than store-bought.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 350°F and line the pan with parchment.
Toast the oats and almonds on a baking sheet until lightly golden.
Melt the butter, honey, and brown sugar together and simmer for 1 minute.
Stir in the vanilla, cinnamon, and salt, then the oats, almonds, and cranberries.
Press the mixture very firmly into the pan and bake until the edges are golden.
Cool completely in the pan before cutting into 12 bars.

title: Ants on a Log
description: Celery, peanut butter, and raisins: the after-school classic.

steps.instructionText: Trim the celery and cut it into 3-inch pieces.
Fill each groove with peanut butter.
Press a line of raisins along the top.

title: Spicy Garlic Edamame
description: Blistered edamame pods tossed in garlic, chili crisp, and soy.

steps.instructionText: Boil the edamame until bright green and hot, then drain well.
Heat the sesame oil in a skillet and blister the pods over high heat.
Add the garlic and stir until fragrant.
Off the heat, toss with the soy sauce, chili crisp, and flaky salt. Serve with a bowl for the empty pods.

title: Hot Spinach Artichoke Dip
description: A bubbling, cheesy dip for chips, crackers, or bread.

ingredients.name: frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
marinated artichoke hearts, drained and chopped

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Beat the cream cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise, and garlic until smooth.
Fold in the spinach, artichokes, Parmesan, half the mozzarella, and the pepper flakes.
Spread in the baking dish and top with the remaining mozzarella.
Bake until bubbling and browned on top.
Serve hot with pita chips.

title: Apple Slices with Peanut Butter Yogurt Dip
description: A protein-packed dip that turns an apple into a proper snack.

steps.instructionText: Whisk the yogurt, peanut butter, honey, and cinnamon until smooth.
Core and slice the apples and toss with the lemon juice to stop them browning.
Serve the apple slices with the dip.

title: Sweet & Salty Trail Mix
description: A make-ahead mix of roasted nuts, seeds, dried fruit, and chocolate.

steps.instructionText: Toss everything together in a large bowl.
Store in an airtight jar for up to a month and portion into ½-cup servings.

title: Baked Kale Chips
description: Crisp, salty kale leaves that disappear as fast as potato chips.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 300°F.
Strip the leaves from the stems, tear into chip-size pieces, then wash and dry completely.
Massage the kale with the oil, nutritional yeast, salt, and garlic powder.
Spread in a single layer over two baking sheets.
Bake until crisp, rotating the sheets halfway through.
Cool on the sheets before serving.

title: Classic Banana Bread
description: A moist, deeply banana-y loaf that uses up overripe fruit.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease the loaf pan.
Mash the bananas and stir in the melted butter.
Mix in the brown sugar, egg, and vanilla, then the baking soda and salt.
Fold in the flour until no streaks remain, then the walnuts.
Bake until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then on a rack before slicing.

title: Soft Pretzel Bites
description: Chewy, golden pretzel nuggets with coarse salt and honey mustard for dipping.

steps.instructionText: Stir the warm water, yeast, and sugar together and let stand until foamy.
Add the flour, salt, and butter and knead with the dough hook until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise until doubled.
Heat the oven to 425°F and bring the boiling water and baking soda to a boil in a large pot.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces, roll each into a rope, and cut into 1-inch bites.
Boil the bites in batches for 30 seconds, lift onto baking sheets, brush with egg, and sprinkle with pretzel salt.
Bake until deep golden brown.
Stir the mustard and honey together for dipping.

title: Strawberry Yogurt Popsicles
description: Creamy swirled freezer pops that are perfect for hot afternoons.

steps.instructionText: Blend half the strawberries with the honey and lemon juice until smooth.
Finely chop the remaining strawberries.
Layer the yogurt, purée, and chopped berries into the molds and swirl gently with a skewer.
Insert the sticks and freeze until solid.
Run the molds under warm water for 10 seconds to release.

title: Pan con Tomate
description: Charred bread rubbed with garlic and grated fresh tomato, finished with olive oil.

steps.instructionText: Halve the tomatoes, grate the cut sides on a box grater, discard the skins, and season the pulp with salt.
Grill or toast the bread until crisp and lightly charred.
Rub the hot toast with the cut garlic clove.
Spoon over the tomato, drizzle with olive oil, and finish with flaky salt.

title: Fresh Spring Rolls with Peanut Sauce
description: Rice paper rolls packed with crisp vegetables, herbs, and tofu.

steps.instructionText: Cook the vermicelli according to the package, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Whisk the peanut butter, hoisin, lime juice, sriracha, and warm water into a smooth sauce.
Dip one rice paper wrapper in warm water for a few seconds until pliable and lay it flat.
Layer on lettuce, noodles, tofu, carrot, cucumber, and herbs, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly. Repeat.
Serve with the peanut sauce.

title: Tzatziki with Baked Pita Chips
description: Cool, garlicky cucumber yogurt dip with crisp homemade pita chips.

steps.instructionText: Grate the cucumber, toss with half the salt, and squeeze out as much liquid as you can in a strainer.
Stir the cucumber into the yogurt with the garlic, dill, lemon juice, and 1 tablespoon of oil, then chill.
While it chills, heat the oven to 400°F, cut each pita into 8 wedges, and toss with the remaining oil, oregano, and salt.
Bake the pita wedges until crisp and golden.
Serve the tzatziki with the chips. It keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

title: Salmon Onigiri
description: Japanese rice balls filled with flaked salted salmon and wrapped in crisp nori.

steps.instructionText: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then cook it with the water.
Meanwhile, sprinkle the salmon with ½ teaspoon of salt, broil until just cooked, then flake it, discarding the skin, and mix with the sesame seeds.
Let the rice rest, then spread it out until cool enough to handle.
Wet your hands, rub them with a little salt, and shape ½ cup of rice around a spoonful of salmon into a triangle. Repeat to make 8.
Wrap each with a nori strip just before eating so it stays crisp.

title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Herb Salmon with Asparagus
description: Salmon and asparagus roasted together on one pan with lemon, garlic, and dill.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 425°F and line the baking sheet with parchment.
Toss the asparagus with 1 tablespoon of the oil and a pinch of salt and roast.
Mix the remaining oil with the garlic, lemon zest, dill, salt, and pepper.
Nestle the salmon among the asparagus, brush with the herb mixture, and roast until the fish flakes easily.
Squeeze the lemon juice over everything and serve.

title: Classic Beef Lasagna
description: Layers of meaty tomato sauce, ricotta, and mozzarella; feeds a crowd and freezes well.

steps.instructionText: Boil the noodles until just short of al dente, then drain and lay flat on oiled foil.
Brown the beef, sausage, and onion in a large skillet, breaking up the meat.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste, then the tomatoes, herbs, and salt, and simmer.
Mix the ricotta, egg, half the Parmesan, and the parsley. Heat the oven to 375°F.
Layer sauce, noodles, ricotta mixture, and mozzarella three times, finishing with sauce, mozzarella, and the remaining Parmesan. You can cover and refrigerate it at this point for up to a day.
Cover with foil and bake.
Uncover and bake until bubbling and browned.
Rest before cutting so the layers hold.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
description: Sichuan-style stir-fry of chicken, peanuts, and dried chilies in a glossy sweet-sour sauce.

steps.instructionText: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, the wine, and 2 teaspoons of cornstarch.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce and cornstarch with the vinegar, sugar, and water.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the chilies and peppercorns until fragrant, without letting them burn.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until cooked through.
Add the garlic, ginger, and scallion whites and stir-fry briefly.
Pour in the sauce and toss until glossy, then add the peanuts and scallion greens.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Chickpea & Spinach Coconut Curry
description: A weeknight chana curry simmered in spiced tomato and coconut milk.

steps.instructionText: Cook the onion in the coconut oil until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, and spices and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk, chickpeas, and salt and simmer until thickened.
Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Finish with lime juice and serve with rice or naan.

title: Sheet-Pan Chicken Fajitas
description: Smoky chicken, peppers, and onions roasted on one pan and piled into warm tortillas.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the chicken, peppers, and onion with the oil, spices, and salt and spread over two baking sheets.
Roast, stirring halfway, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are charred at the edges.
Wrap the tortillas in foil and warm them in the oven for the last few minutes.
Squeeze the lime over the pan and serve with the tortillas, sour cream, and cilantro.

title: Shrimp & Chorizo Paella
description: Saffron rice with shrimp, chorizo, and peas, cooked until it forms a crisp socarrat.

steps.instructionText: Warm the stock with the saffron.
Brown the chorizo in the oil, then lift it out.
Cook the onion and pepper in the same pan until soft.
Add the garlic, paprika, and tomatoes and cook until thick.
Stir in the rice, then add the stock, salt, and chorizo. Bring to a boil, then simmer without stirring.
Press the shrimp into the rice, scatter over the peas, and cook until the shrimp are pink and the liquid is absorbed.
Turn up the heat until the rice crackles, to form a crisp crust underneath.
Cover with a towel and rest, then serve with lemon wedges and parsley.

title: Homemade Margherita Pizza
description: Chewy homemade crust topped with crushed tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and basil.

steps.instructionText: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, water, and 1 tablespoon of oil and knead until smooth.
Cover and let rise until doubled.
Meanwhile, put the pizza stone in the oven and heat to 500°F for at least 45 minutes.
Divide the dough in two and stretch each half into a 12-inch round on a cornmeal-dusted peel.
Spread with the tomatoes, season with salt, and scatter over the mozzarella.
Slide onto the stone and bake one pizza at a time until blistered.
Top with basil and a drizzle of the remaining oil.

title: Chicken Katsu Curry
description: Crispy panko chicken cutlets with a rich, mild Japanese curry sauce over rice.

steps.instructionText: Rinse the rice and start it cooking with its water.
Cook the onion in 1 tablespoon of the oil until soft.
Add the carrots, potatoes, and curry water and simmer until tender.
Stir in the curry roux until dissolved and simmer until thick.
Meanwhile, butterfly and pound the chicken to an even thickness, season with salt, and coat in flour, then beaten egg, then panko.
Fry the cutlets in the remaining oil until golden and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side, in batches.
Rest the cutlets, then slice.
Serve the sliced katsu over the rice with the curry sauce spooned alongside.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Apricots
description: Chicken thighs braised with warm spices, apricots, and olives, served over fluffy couscous.

steps.instructionText: Season the chicken with half the spices and salt.
Brown the chicken skin-side down in the oil, in batches, then set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pan until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger, and remaining spices and stir until fragrant.
Add the broth, apricots, and honey, return the chicken skin-side up, cover, and simmer gently.
Add the olives and lemon juice and simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens.
Meanwhile, pour the boiling water over the couscous with a pinch of salt, cover for 5 minutes, and fluff.
Serve the tagine over the couscous with cilantro and almonds. It tastes even better the next day.
